s: a specialty roaster living up to its name in a quiet Les Corts corner
w: A specialty coffee roaster and café on a residential corner of Les Corts, well away from the Gothic Quarter crowds -- own-roasted beans, precise preparation, and a calm room built for lingering with a laptop or a book rather than passing through. One of several branches, but this one keeps the low-key, neighbourhood feel the name promises.
_facts: Located at Carrer de Déu i Mata, corner Carrer de Constança, 08029 Barcelona, Les Corts
Specialty coffee roaster with its own roastery in Sant Martí and several Barcelona café branches
Also known for reviving Granja Hidden, a historic Barcelona granja/café format

s: a former carpentry workshop turned coffee-and-art space in El Raval
w: A calm coffee bar behind the surviving wooden doors of a former carpentry workshop on a quiet Raval street -- some of the old timber recycled into the furniture, a graffiti mural at the entrance, and regular small art shows and live music keeping the workshop's creative use alive. Coffee roasted locally by Slow Mov, brewed with attention rather than spectacle.
_facts: Located at Carrer de la Verge 1, 08001 Barcelona, El Raval
Housed in a former carpentry workshop, with recycled timber used in the furniture
Serves coffee roasted by Barcelona roaster Slow Mov
Hosts occasional art exhibitions and live music events

s: a restored 1882 iron-framed market hall with more locals than tourists
w: A grand iron-framed covered market from 1882, closed for a lengthy restoration and reopened with its Modernista-adjacent structure and light intact. Stalls of fresh produce, seafood, cured meats and takeaway food serve a neighbourhood crowd that still outnumbers visitors -- the everyday counterpart to La Boqueria's tourist theatre, a short walk from the Eixample grid.
_facts: Located at Carrer del Comte d'Urgell 1, 08011 Barcelona, Sant Antoni
Underwent a long restoration/renovation, reopening the main food hall in 2018
Serves the Sant Antoni neighbourhood with a strong local, non-touristy customer base

s: a Modernista market hall at the heart of Gràcia's village-like centre
w: A Modernista iron-and-glass market hall at Plaça de la Llibertat, in the middle of Gràcia -- the district that still carries itself like an independent town annexed into Barcelona rather than just another neighbourhood. Traditional stalls and a slower, plaza-centred rhythm reward a wander north of the Eixample grid.
_facts: Located at Plaça de la Llibertat 27, 08012 Barcelona, Vila de Gràcia
Serves the Gràcia neighbourhood, historically an independent town before annexation to Barcelona in 1897
Reachable via Fontana metro station (L3) or the Gràcia FGC station
